Even upon the fabric of time,
Where purple becomes orange
And orange purple,
This life glowed,
A dire red stain, indelible;
Yet when he was dead,
He saw that he had not lived.

book.title: The Black Riders and Other Lines

poems.title: LXIII. There was a great cathedral
poems.author: Stephen Crane
lines: There was a great cathedral.
To solemn songs,
A white procession
Moved toward the altar.
The chief man there
Was erect, and bore himself proudly.
Yet some could see him cringe,
As in a place of danger,
Throwing frightened glances into the air,
A-start at threatening faces of the past.

book.title: The Black Riders and Other Lines

poems.title: LXIV. Friend, your white beard sweeps the ground
poems.author: Stephen Crane
lines: Friend, your white beard sweeps the ground,
Why do you stand, expectant?
Do you hope to see it
In one of your withered days?
With your old eyes
Do you hope to see
The triumphal march of Justice?
Do not wait, friend
Take your white beard
And your old eyes
To more tender lands.

book.title: The Black Riders and Other Lines

poems.title: LXV. Once, I knew a fine song
poems.author: Stephen Crane
lines: Once, I knew a fine song,
--It is true, believe me,--
It was all of birds,
And I held them in a basket;
When I opened the wicket,
Heavens!  They all flew away.
I cried, "Come back, little thoughts!"
But they only laughed.
They flew on
Until they were as sand
Thrown between me and the sky.

book.title: The Black Riders and Other Lines

poems.title: LXVI. If I should cast off this tattered coat
poems.author: Stephen Crane
lines: If I should cast off this tattered coat,
And go free into the mighty sky;
If I should find nothing there
But a vast blue,
Echoless, ignorant,--
What then?

book.title: The Black Riders and Other Lines

poems.title: Stray Birds 1
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Stray birds of summer come to my window to sing and fly away.
And yellow leaves of autumn, which have no songs, flutter and fall there with a sigh.

poems.title: Stray Birds 2
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: O troupe of little vagrants of the world, leave your footprints in my words.

poems.title: Stray Birds 3
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world puts off its mask of vastness to its lover.
It becomes small as one song, as one kiss of the eternal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 4
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: It is the tears of the earth that keep her smiles in bloom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 5
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The mighty desert is burning for the love of a blade of grass who shakes her head and laughs and flies away.

poems.title: Stray Birds 6
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 7
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sands in your way beg for your song and your movement, dancing water.  Will you carry the burden of their lameness?

poems.title: Stray Birds 8
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Her wistful face haunts my dreams like the rain at night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 9
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Once we dreamt that we were strangers.
We wake up to find that we were dear to each other.

poems.title: Stray Birds 10
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Sorrow is hushed into peace in my heart like the evening among the silent trees.

poems.title: Stray Birds 11
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Some unseen fingers, like idle breeze, are playing upon my heart the music of the ripples.

poems.title: Stray Birds 12
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "What language is thine, O sea?"
"The language of eternal question."
"What language is thy answer, O sky?
"The language of eternal silence."

poems.title: Stray Birds 13
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Listen, my heart, to the whispers of the world with which it makes love to you.

poems.title: Stray Birds 14
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The mystery of creation is like the darkness of night--it is great.  Delusions of knowledge are like the fog of the morning.

poems.title: Stray Birds 15
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Do not seat your love upon a precipice because it is high.

poems.title: Stray Birds 16
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I sit at my window this morning where the world like a passer-by stops for a moment, nods to me and goes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 17
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: These little thoughts are the rustle of leaves; they have their whisper of joy in my mind.

poems.title: Stray Birds 18
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: What you are you do not see, what you see is your shadow.

poems.title: Stray Birds 19
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My wishes are fools, they shout across thy songs, my Master.
Let me but listen.

poems.title: Stray Birds 20
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I cannot choose the best.
The best chooses me.

poems.title: Stray Birds 21
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: They throw their shadows before them who carry their lantern on their back.

poems.title: Stray Birds 22
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 23
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "We, the rustling leaves, have a voice that answers the storms, but who are you so silent?"
"I am a mere flower."

poems.title: Stray Birds 24
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Rest belongs to the work as the eyelids to the eyes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 25
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man is a born child, his power is the power of growth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 26
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God expects answers for the flowers he sends us, not for the sun and the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 27
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The light that plays, like a naked child, among the green leaves happily knows not that man can lie.

poems.title: Stray Birds 28
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: O Beauty, find thyself in love, not in the flattery of thy mirror.

poems.title: Stray Birds 29
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My heart beats her waves at the shore of the world and writes upon it her signature in tears with the words, "I love thee."

poems.title: Stray Birds 30
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "Moon, for what do you wait?"
"To salute the sun for whom I must make way."

poems.title: Stray Birds 31
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The trees come up to my window like the yearning voice of the dumb earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 32
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: His own mornings are new surprises to God.

poems.title: Stray Birds 33
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Life finds its wealth by the claims of the world, and its worth by the claims of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 34
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The dry river-bed finds no thanks for its past.

poems.title: Stray Birds 35
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The bird wishes it were a cloud.  The cloud wishes it were a bird.

poems.title: Stray Birds 36
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The waterfall sings, "I find my song, when I find my freedom."

poems.title: Stray Birds 37
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I cannot tell why this heart languishes in silence.
It is for small needs it never asks, or knows or remembers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 38
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Woman, when you move about in your household service your limbs sing like a hill stream among its pebbles.

poems.title: Stray Birds 39
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sun goes to cross the Western sea, leaving its last salutation to the East.

poems.title: Stray Birds 40
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Do not blame your food because you have no appetite.

poems.title: Stray Birds 41
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The trees, like the longings of the earth, stand a-tiptoe to peep at the heaven.

poems.title: Stray Birds 42
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: You smiled and talked to me of nothing and I felt that for this I had been waiting long.

poems.title: Stray Birds 43
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The fish in the water is silent, the animal on the earth is noisy, the bird in the air is singing, But Man has in him the silence of the sea, the noise of the earth and the music of the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 44
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world rushes on over the strings of the lingering heart making the music of sadness.

poems.title: Stray Birds 45
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: He has made his weapons his gods.  When his weapons win he is defeated himself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 46
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God finds himself by creating.

poems.title: Stray Birds 47
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Shadow, with her veil drawn, follows Light in secret meekness, with her silent steps of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 48
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The stars are not afraid to appear like fireflies.

poems.title: Stray Birds 49
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I thank thee that I am none of the wheels of power but I am one with the living creatures that are crushed by it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 50
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The mind, sharp but not broad, sticks at every point but does not move.

poems.title: Stray Birds 51
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Your idol is shattered in the dust to prove that God's dust is greater than your idol.

poems.title: Stray Birds 52
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man does not reveal himself in his history, he struggles up through it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 53
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: While the glass lamp rebukes the earthen for calling it cousin, the moon rises, and the glass lamp, with a bland smile, calls her, "My dear, dear sister."

poems.title: Stray Birds 54
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Like the meeting of the seagulls and the waves we meet and come near.  The seagulls fly off, the waves roll away and we depart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 55
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My day is done, and I am like a boat drawn on the beach, listening to the dance-music of the tide in the evening.

poems.title: Stray Birds 56
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Life is given to us, we earn it by giving it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 57
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: We come nearest to the great when we are great in humility.

poems.title: Stray Birds 58
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.

poems.title: Stray Birds 59
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Never be afraid of the moments--thus sings the voice of the everlasting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 60
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The hurricane seeks the shortest road by the no-road, and suddenly ends its search in the Nowhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 61
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Take my wine in my own cup, friend.
It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.

poems.title: Stray Birds 62
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The Perfect decks itself in beauty for the love of the Imperfect.

poems.title: Stray Birds 63
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God says to man, "I heal you therefore I hurt, love you therefore punish."

poems.title: Stray Birds 64
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.

poems.title: Stray Birds 65
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.

poems.title: Stray Birds 66
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The infant flower opens its bud and cries, "Dear World, please do not fade."

poems.title: Stray Birds 67
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God grows weary of great kingdoms, but never of little flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 68
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.

poems.title: Stray Birds 69
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."

poems.title: Stray Birds 70
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Where is the fountain that throws up these flowers in a ceaseless outbreak of ecstasy?

poems.title: Stray Birds 71
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree.
The tree gave it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 72
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: In my solitude of heart I feel the sigh of this widowed evening veiled with mist and rain.

poems.title: Stray Birds 73
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Chastity is a wealth that comes from abundance of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 74
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The mist, like love, plays upon the heart of the hills and brings out surprises of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 75
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.

poems.title: Stray Birds 76
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The poet wind is out over the sea and the forest to seek his own voice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 77
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 78
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth.
The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 79
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man barricades against himself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 80
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Your voice, my friend, wanders in my heart, like the muffled sound of the sea among these listening pines.

poems.title: Stray Birds 81
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: What is this unseen flame of darkness whose sparks are the stars?

poems.title: Stray Birds 82
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 83
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.

poems.title: Stray Birds 84
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: In death the many becomes one; in life the one becomes many.
Religion will be one when God is dead.

poems.title: Stray Birds 85
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The artist is the lover of Nature, therefore he is her slave and her master.

poems.title: Stray Birds 86
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "How far are you from me, O Fruit?"
"I am hidden in your heart, O Flower."

poems.title: Stray Birds 87
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This longing is for the one who is felt in the dark, but not seen in the day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 88
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "You are the big drop of dew under the lotus leaf, I am the smaller one on its upper side," said the dewdrop to the lake.

poems.title: Stray Birds 89
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.

poems.title: Stray Birds 90
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: In darkness the One appears as uniform; in the light the One appears as manifold.

poems.title: Stray Birds 91
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The great earth makes herself hospitable with the help of the grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 92
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The birth and death of the leaves are the rapid whirls of the eddy whose wider circles move slowly among stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 93
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Power said to the world, "You are mine.
The world kept it prisoner on her throne.
Love said to the world, "I am thine."
The world gave it the freedom of her house.

poems.title: Stray Birds 94
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The mist is like the earth's desire.  It hides the sun for whom she cries.

poems.title: Stray Birds 95
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Be still, my heart, these great trees are prayers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 96
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The noise of the moment scoffs at the music of the Eternal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 97
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.

poems.title: Stray Birds 98
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 99
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.

poems.title: Stray Birds 100
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky.
The morning crowned it with splendour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 101
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 102
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 103
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Roots are the branches down in the earth.
Branches are roots in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 104
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The music of the far-away summer flutters around the Autumn seeking its former nest.

poems.title: Stray Birds 105
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 106
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The touch of the nameless days clings to my heart like mosses round the old tree.

poems.title: Stray Birds 107
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The echo mocks her origin to prove she is the original.

poems.title: Stray Birds 108
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God is ashamed when the prosperous boasts of His special favour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 109
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 110
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 111
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: That which ends in exhaustion is death, but the perfect ending is in the endless.

poems.title: Stray Birds 112
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sun has his simple robe of light.  The clouds are decked with gorgeousness.

poems.title: Stray Birds 113
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The hills are like shouts of children who raise their arms, trying to catch stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 114
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.

poems.title: Stray Birds 115
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The power that boasts of its mischiefs is laughed at by the yellow leaves that fall, and clouds that pass by.

poems.title: Stray Birds 116
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The earth hums to me to-day in the sun, like a woman at her spinng, some ballad of the ancient time in a forgotten tongue.

poems.title: Stray Birds 117
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The grass-blade is worth of the great world where it grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 118
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Dream is a wife who must talk.
Sleep is a husband who silently suffers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 119
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The night kisses the fading day whispering to his ear, "I am death, your mother.  I am to give you fresh birth."

poems.title: Stray Birds 120
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I feel, thy beauty, dark night, like that of the loved woman when she has put out the lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 121
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 122
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Dear friend, I feel the silence of your great thoughts of may a deepening eventide on this beach when I listen to these waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 123
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The bird thinks it is an act of kindness to give the fish a lift in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 124
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "In the moon thou sendest thy love letters to me," said the night to the sun.
"I leave my answers in tears upon the grass."

poems.title: Stray Birds 125
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The Great is a born child; when he dies he gives his great childhood to the world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 126
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.

poems.title: Stray Birds 127
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave.
The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.

poems.title: Stray Birds 128
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 129
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Asks the Possible to the Impossible, "Where is your dwelling place?"
"In the dreams of the impotent," comes the answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 130
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.

poems.title: Stray Birds 131
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I hear some rustle of things behind my sadness of heart,--I cannot see them.

poems.title: Stray Birds 132
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Leisure in its activity is work.
The stillness of the sea stirs in waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 133
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The leaf becomes flower when it loves.
The flower becomes fruit when it worships.

poems.title: Stray Birds 134
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.

poems.title: Stray Birds 135
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This rainy evening the wind is restless.
I look at the swaying branches and ponder over the greatness of all things.

poems.title: Stray Birds 136
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Storm of midnight, like a giant child awakened in the untimely dark, has begun to play and shout.

poems.title: Stray Birds 137
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thou raisest thy waves vainly to follow thy lover.  O sea, thou lonely bride of the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 138
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "I am ashamed of my emptiness," said the Word to the Work.
"I know how poor I am when I see you," said the Work to the Word.

poems.title: Stray Birds 139
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 140
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Truth in her dress finds facts too tight.
In fiction she moves with ease.

poems.title: Stray Birds 141
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 142
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.

poems.title: Stray Birds 143
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Woman, with the grace of your fingers you touched my things and order came out like music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 144
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years.
It sings to me in the night,--"I loved you."

poems.title: Stray Birds 145
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The flaming fire warns me off by its own glow.
Save me from the dying embers hidden under ashes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 146
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.

poems.title: Stray Birds 147
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The dust of the dead words clings to thee.
Wash thy soul with silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 148
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 149
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world has opened its heart of light in the morning.
Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 150
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My thoughts shimmer with these shimmering leaves and my heart sings with the touch of this sunlight; my life is glad to be floating with all things into the blue of space, into the dark of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 151
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 152
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This is a dream in which things are all loose and they oppress.
I shall find them gathered in thee when I awake and shall be free.

poems.title: Stray Birds 153
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "Who is there to take up my duties?"  asked the setting sun.
"I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 154
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.

poems.title: Stray Birds 155
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Silence will carry your voice like the nest that holds the sleeping birds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 156
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The Great walks with the Small without fear.
The Middling keeps aloof.

poems.title: Stray Birds 157
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The night opens the flowers in secret and allows the day to get thanks.

poems.title: Stray Birds 158
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Power takes as ingratitude the writhings of its victims.

poems.title: Stray Birds 159
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 160
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The raindrops kissed the earth and whispered,--"We are thy homesick children, mother, come back to thee from the heaven."

poems.title: Stray Birds 161
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The cobweb pretends to catch dew-drops and catches flies.

poems.title: Stray Birds 162
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Love!  when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.

poems.title: Stray Birds 163
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "The learned say that your lights will one day be no more."  said the firefly to the stars.
The stars made no answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 164
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: In the dusk of the evening the bird of some early dawn comes to the nest of my silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 165
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thoughts pass in my mind like flocks of ducks in the sky.
I hear the voice of their wings.

poems.title: Stray Birds 166
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The canal loves to think that rivers exist solely to supply it with water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 167
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 168
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: That which oppresses me, is it my soul trying to come out in the open, or the soul of the world knocking at my heart for its entrance?

poems.title: Stray Birds 169
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thought feeds itself with its own words and grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 170
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have dipped the vessel of my heart into this silent hour; it has filled with love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 171
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Either you have work or you have not.
When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.

poems.title: Stray Birds 172
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sunflower blushed to own the nameless flower as her kin.
The sun rose and smiled on it, saying, "Are you well, my darling?"

poems.title: Stray Birds 173
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "Who drives me forward like fate?"
"The Myself striding on my back."

poems.title: Stray Birds 174
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The clouds fill the watercups of the river, hiding themselves in the distant hills.

poems.title: Stray Birds 175
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 176
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark.
The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 177
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Your smile was the flowers of your own fields, your talk was the rustle of your own mountain pines, but your heart was the woman that we all know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 178
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,-- great things are for everyone.

poems.title: Stray Birds 179
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Woman, thou hast encircled the world's heart with the depth of thy tears as the sea has the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 180
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The sunshine greets me with a smile.  The rain, his sad sister, talks to my heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 181
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten.
In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.

poems.title: Stray Birds 182
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I am like the road in the night listening to the footfalls of its memories in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 183
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The evening sky to me is like a window, and a lighted lamp, and a waiting behind it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 184
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.

poems.title: Stray Birds 185
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 186
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: They hated and killed and men praised them.
But God in shame hastens to hide its memory under the green grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 187
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Toes are the fingers that have forsaken their past.

poems.title: Stray Birds 188
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 189
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The pet dog suspects the universe for scheming to take its place.

poems.title: Stray Birds 190
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust.
Let the world find its way to you.

poems.title: Stray Birds 191
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth--"Your freedom is mine."

poems.title: Stray Birds 192
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Woman, in your laughter you have the music of the fountain of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 193
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: A mind all logic is like a knife all blade.
It makes the hand bleed that uses it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 194
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God loves man's lamp lights better than his own great stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 195
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This world is the world of wild storms kept tame with the music of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 196
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "My heart is like the golden casket of thy kiss," said the sunset cloud to the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 197
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.

poems.title: Stray Birds 198
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The cricket's chirp and the patter of rain come to me through the dark, like the rustle of dreams from my past youth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 199
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "I have lost my dewdrop," cries the flower to the morning sky that has lost all its stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 200
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The burning log bursts in flame and cries,--"This is my flower, my death."

poems.title: Stray Birds 201
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small.
His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.

poems.title: Stray Birds 202
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river.
"Let me keep your footprints in my heart."

poems.title: Stray Birds 203
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The day, with the noise of this little earth, drowns the silence of all worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 204
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The song feels the infinite in the air, the picture in the earth, the poem in the air and the earth; For its words have meaning that walks and music that soars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 205
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: When the sun goes down to the West, the East of his morning stands before him in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 206
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.

poems.title: Stray Birds 207
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 208
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.

poems.title: Stray Birds 209
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Maiden, your simplicity, like the blueness of the lake, reveals your depth of truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 210
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The best does not come alone.  It comes with the company of the all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 211
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God's right hand is gentle, but terrible is his left hand.

poems.title: Stray Birds 212
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My evening came among the alien trees and spoke in a language which my morning stars did not know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 213
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with the gold of the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 214
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 215
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God waits to win back his own flowers as gifts from man's hands.

poems.title: Stray Birds 216
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.

poems.title: Stray Birds 217
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.

poems.title: Stray Birds 218
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My heart has spread its sails to the idle winds for the shadowy island of Anywhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 219
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.

poems.title: Stray Birds 220
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Make me thy cup and let my fulness be for thee and for thine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 221
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The storm is like the cry of some god in pain whose love the earth refuses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 222
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world does not leak because death is not a crack.

poems.title: Stray Birds 223
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.

poems.title: Stray Birds 224
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My friend, your great heart shone with the sunrise of the East like the snowy summit of a lonely hill in the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 225
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The fountain of death makes the still water of life play.

poems.title: Stray Birds 226
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Those who have everything but thee, my God, laugh at those who have nothing but thyself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 227
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The movement of life has its rest in its own music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 228
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 229
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.

poems.title: Stray Birds 230
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.

poems.title: Stray Birds 231
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 232
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The same lotus of our clime blooms here in the alien water with the same sweetness, under another name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 233
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: In heart's perspective the distance looms large.

poems.title: Stray Birds 234
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 235
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday.  See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 236
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Smoke boasts to the sky, and Ashes to the earth, that they are brothers to the fire.

poems.title: Stray Birds 237
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever."
The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 238
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me.
I am a poet.

poems.title: Stray Birds 239
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The dim silence of my mind seems filled with crickets' chirp--the grey twilight of sound.

poems.title: Stray Birds 240
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Rockets, your insult to the stars follows yourself back to the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 241
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness.
I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 242
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship.
In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 243
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 244
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 245
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The bird-song is the echo of the morning light back from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 246
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "Are you too proud to kiss me?"  the morning light asks the buttercup.

poems.title: Stray Birds 247
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: "How may I sing to thee and worship, O Sun?"  asked the little flower.
"By the simple silence of thy purity," answered the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 248
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man is worse than an animal when he is an animal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 249
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Dark clouds become heaven's flowers when kissed by light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 250
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.

poems.title: Stray Birds 251
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The night's silence, like a deep lamp, is burning with the light of its milky way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 252
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Around the sunny island of Life swells day and night death's limitless song of the sea.

poems.title: Stray Birds 253
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Is not this mountain like a flower, with its petals of hills, drinking the sunlight?

poems.title: Stray Birds 254
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 255
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 256
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The eyes are not proud of their sight but of their eyeglasses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 257
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less.  Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 258
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.

poems.title: Stray Birds 259
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: My heart, with its lapping waves of song, longs to caress this green world of the sunny day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 260
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Wayside grass, love the star, then your dreams will come out in flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 261
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let your music, like a sword, pierce the noise of the market to its heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 262
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The trembling leaves of this tree touch my heart like the fingers of an infant child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 263
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: This sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 264
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The little flower lies in the dust.
It sought the path of the butterfly.

poems.title: Stray Birds 265
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I am in the world of the roads.  The night comes.  Open thy gate, thou world of the home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 266
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have sung the songs of thy day.  In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.

poems.title: Stray Birds 267
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I do not ask thee into the house.
Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.

poems.title: Stray Birds 268
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Death belongs to life as birth does.  The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.

poems.title: Stray Birds 269
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine--teach me to know thy words in pain and death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 270
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The night's flower was late when the morning kissed her, she shivered and sighed and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 271
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 272
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 273
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 274
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Light in my heart the evening star of rest and then let the night whisper to me of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 275
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I am a child in the dark.
I stretch my hands through the coverlet of night for thee, Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 276
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The day of work is done.  Hide my face in your arms, Mother.
Let me dream.

poems.title: Stray Birds 277
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 278
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."

poems.title: Stray Birds 279
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: We live in this world when we love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 280
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 281
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have seen thee as the half-awakened child sees his mother in the dusk of the dawn and then smiles and sleeps again.

poems.title: Stray Birds 282
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.

poems.title: Stray Birds 283
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.

poems.title: Stray Birds 284
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 285
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: They light their own lamps and sing their own words in their temples.
But the birds sing thy name in thine own morning light,--for thy name is joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 286
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Lead me in the centre of thy silence to fill my heart with songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 287
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let them live who choose in their own hissing world of fireworks.
My heart longs for thy stars, my God.

poems.title: Stray Birds 288
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 289
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Put out the lamp when thou wishest.
I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 290
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.

poems.title: Stray Birds 291
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Some day I shall sing to thee in the sunrise of some other world, "I have seen thee before in the light of the earth, in the love of man."

poems.title: Stray Birds 292
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 293
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.

poems.title: Stray Birds 294
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.

poems.title: Stray Birds 295
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Truth seems to come with its final word; and the final word gives birth to its next.

poems.title: Stray Birds 296
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 297
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Sweetness of thy name fills my heart when I forget mine--like thy morning sun when the mist is melted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 298
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The silent night has the beauty of the mother and the clamorous day of the child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 299
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The world loved man when he smiled.  The world became afraid of him when he laughed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 300
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God waits for man to regain his childhood in wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 301
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let me feel this world as thy love taking form, then my love will help it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 302
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 303
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God kisses the finite in his love and man the infinite.

poems.title: Stray Birds 304
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.

poems.title: Stray Birds 305
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God's silence ripens man's thoughts into speech.

poems.title: Stray Birds 306
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Thou wilt find, Eternal Traveller, marks of thy footsteps across my songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 307
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let me not shame thee, Father, who displayest thy glory in thy children.

poems.title: Stray Birds 308
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world.  But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.

poems.title: Stray Birds 309
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: To-night there is a stir among the palm leaves, a swell in the sea, Full Moon, like the heart throb of the world.  From what unknown sky hast thou carried in thy silence the aching secret of love?

poems.title: Stray Birds 310
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I dream of a star, an island of light, where I shall be born and in the depth of its quickening leisure my life will ripen its works like the ricefield in the autumn sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 311
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The smell of the wet earth in the rain rises like a great chant of praise from the voiceless multitude of the insignificant.

poems.title: Stray Birds 312
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 313
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 314
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 315
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: When all the strings of my life will be tuned, my Master, then at every touch of thine will come out the music of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 316
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.

poems.title: Stray Birds 317
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 318
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I feel thy gaze upon my heart this moment like the sunny silence of the morning upon the lonely field whose harvest is over.

poems.title: Stray Birds 319
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I long for the Island of Songs across this heaving Sea of Shouts.

poems.title: Stray Birds 320
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: The prelude of the night is commenced in the music of the sunset, in its solemn hymn to the ineffable dark.

poems.title: Stray Birds 321
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height.  Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 322
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Things look phantastic in this dimness of the dusk--the spires whose bases are lost in the dark and tree tops like blots of ink.
I shall wait for the morning and wake up to see thy city in the light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 323
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 324
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent.  They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 325
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.

poems.title: Stray Birds 326
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
lines: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.

poems.title: Composed by the commander of the forces of the Mikado Zhiyomei
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: The long spring day is o'er, and dark despond
My heart invades, and lets the tears flow down,
As all alone I stand, when from beyond
The mount our heav'n-sent monarch's throne doth crown.
There breathes the twilight wind and turns my sleeve.
Ah, gentle breeze! to turn, home to return,
Is all my prayer; I cannot cease to grieve
On this long toilsome road; I burn, I burn!
Yes! the poor heart I used to think so brave
Is all afire, though none the flame may see,
Like to the salt-kilns there by Tsunu's wave,
Where toil the fisher-maidens wearily.
Anon.

poems.title: Love Is Pain
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: 'Twas said of old, and still the ages say,
"The lover's path is full of doubt and woe."
Of me they spake: I know not, nor can know,
If she I sigh for will my love repay.
My heart sinks on my breast; with bitter strife
My heart is torn, and grief she cannot see.
All unavailing is this agony
To help the love that has become my life.
Anon.

poems.title: No Tidings
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: The year has come, the year has gone again,
And still no tidings of mine absent love!
Through the long days of spring all heaven above
And earth beneath, re-echo with my pain.
In dark cocoon my mother's silk-worms dwell;
Like them, a captive, through the livelong day
Alone I sit and sigh my soul away,
For ne'er to any I my love may tell.
Like to the pine-trees I must stand and pine,
While downward slanting fall the shades of night,
Till my long sleeve of purest snowy white,
With showers of tears, is steeped in bitter brine.
Anon.

poems.title: Homeward
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: From Kaminabi's crest
The clouds descending pour in sheeted rain,
And, 'midst the gloom, the wind sighs o'er the plain:--
Oh! he that sadly press'd,
Leaving my loving side, alone to roam
Magami's des'late moor, has he reached home?
Anon.

poems.title: The Maiden and the Dog
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: As the bold huntsman on some mountain path
Waits for the stag he hopes may pass that way,
So wait I for my love both night and day:--
Then bark not at him, as thou fearest my wrath.
Anon.

poems.title: Love Is All
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Where in spring the sweetest flowers
Fill Mount Kaminabi's bowers,
Where in autumn dyed with red,
Each ancient maple rears its head,
And Aska's flood, with sedges lin'd,
As a belt the mound doth bind:--
There see my heart--a reed that sways,
Nor aught but love's swift stream obeys,
And now, if like the dew, dear maid,
Life must fade, then let it fade:--
My secret love is not in vain,
For thou lov'st me back again.

poems.title: He Comes Not
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: He comes not! 'tis in vain I wait;
The crane's wild cry strikes on mine ear,
The tempest howls, the hour is late,
Dark is the raven night and drear:--
And, as I thus stand sighing,
The snowflakes round me flying
Light on my sleeve, and freeze it crisp and clear.
Sure 'tis too late! he cannot come;
Yet trust I still that we may meet,
As sailors gayly rowing home
Trust in their ship so safe and fleet.
Though waking hours conceal him,
Oh! may my dreams reveal him,
Filling the long, long night with converse sweet!
Anon.

poems.title: A Damsel Crossing a Bridge
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Across the bridge, with scarlet lacquer glowing,
That o'er the Katashiha's stream is laid,
All trippingly a tender girl is going,
In bodice blue and crimson skirt arrayed.
None to escort her: would that I were knowing
Whether alone she sleeps on virgin bed,
Or if some spouse has won her by his wooing:--
Tell me her house! I'll ask the pretty maid!
Anon.

poems.title: Secret Love
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: If as my spirit yearns for thine
Thine yearns for mine, why thus delay?
And yet, what answer might be mine
If, pausing on her way,
Some gossip bade me tell
Whence the deep sighs that from my bosom swell?
And thy dear name my lips should pass,
My blushes would our love declare;
No, no! I'll say my longing was
To see the moon appear
O'er yonder darkling hill;
Yet 'tis on thee mine eyes would gaze their fill.
Anon.

poems.title: The Omen[143]
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Yes! 'twas the hour when all my hopes
Seemed idle as the dews that shake
And tremble in their lotus-cups
By deep Tsurugi's lake--
'Twas then the omen said:--
"Fear not! he'll come his own dear love to wed."
What though my mother bids me flee
Thy fond embrace? No heed I take;
As pure, as deep my love for thee
As Kiyosumi's lake.
One thought fills all my heart:--
When wilt thou come no more again to part?
Anon.

poems.title: Rain and Snow
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Forever on Mikane's crest,
That soars so far away,
The rain it rains in ceaseless sheets,
The snow it snows all day.
And ceaseless as the rain and snow
That fall from heaven above,
So ceaselessly, since first we met,
I love my darling love.
Anon.

poems.title: Mount Mikash
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Oft in the misty spring
The vapors roll o'er Mount Mikash's crest,
While, pausing not to rest,
The birds each morn with plaintive note do sing.
Like to the mists of spring
My heart is rent; for, like the song of birds,
Still all unanswered ring
The tender accents of my passionate words.
I call her ev'ry day
Till daylight fades away;
I call her ev'ry night
Till dawn restores the light;--
But my fond prayers are all too weak to bring
My darling back to sight.
Akahito.

poems.title: By One of His Ladies
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Alas! poor mortal maid! unfit to hold
High converse with the glorious gods above,
Each morn that breaks still finds me unconsoled,
Each hour still hears me sighing for thy love.
Wert thou a precious stone, I'd clasp thee tight
Around mine arm; wert thou a silken dress
I'd ne'er discard thee, either day or night:--
Last night, sweet love! I dreamt I saw thy face.

poems.title: Short Stanza on the Same Occasion
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: So young, so young! he cannot know the way:--
On Hades' porter I'll a bribe bestow,
That on his shoulders the dear infant may
Be safely carried to the realms below.
Attributed to Okura.
FOOTNOTES:
[Footnote 144: Died A.D. 671.]
[Footnote 145: Viz., with the departed and deified Mikado.]
[Footnote 146: The Milky Way.]
[Footnote 147: The part played by the mirror in the devotions of the
Japanese is carried back by them to a tale in their mythology which
relates the disappearance into a cavern of the Sun-goddess Amaterasu,
and the manner in which she was enticed forth by being led to believe
that her reflection in a mirror that was shown to her was another
deity more lovely than herself.]

poems.title: Composed by the Mikado Zhiyomei
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Countless are the mountain-chains
Tow'ring o'er Cipango's plains;
But fairest is Mount Kago's peak,
Whose heav'nward soaring heights I seek,
And gaze on all my realms beneath--
Gaze on the land where vapors wreath
O'er many a cot; gaze on the sea,
Where cry the sea-gulls merrily.
Yes! 'tis a very pleasant land,
Fill'd with joys on either hand,
Sweeter than aught beneath the sky,
Dear islands of the dragon-fly!

poems.title: The Mikado'S Bow[149]
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: When the dawn is shining,
He takes it up and fondles it with pride;
When the day's declining,
He lays it by his pillow's side.
Hark to the twanging of the string!
This is the Bow of our great Lord and King!
Now to the morning chase they ride,
Now to the chase again at eventide:
Hark to the twanging of the string!
This is the Bow of our great Lord and King!
Hashibito.

poems.title: Spring and Autumn
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: When winter turns to spring,
Birds that were songless make their songs resound,
Flow'rs that were flow'rless cover all the ground;
Yet 'tis no perfect thing:--
I cannot walk, so tangled is each hill;
So thick the herbs I cannot pluck my fill.
But in the autumn-tide
I cull the scarlet leaves and love them dear,
And let the green leaves stay, with many a tear,
All on the fair hill-side:--
No time so sweet as that. Away! Away!
Autumn's the time I fain would keep alway.
Ohogimi.

poems.title: Spring
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: When winter turns to spring,
The dews of morn in pearly radiance lie,
The mists of eve rise circling to the sky,
And Kaminabi's thickets ring
With the sweet notes the nightingale doth sing.
Anon.

poems.title: Recollections of My Children
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Ne'er a melon can I eat,
But calls to mind my children dear;
Ne'er a chestnut crisp and sweet,
But makes the lov'd ones seem more near.
Whence did they come, my life to cheer?
Before mine eyes they seem to sweep,
So that I may not even sleep.
What use to me the gold and silver hoard?
What use to me the gems most rich and rare?
Brighter by far--aye! bright beyond compare--
The joys my children to my heart afford!
Yamagami-no Okura.

poems.title: The Brook of Hatsuse
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Pure is Hatsuse mountain-brook--
So pure it mirrors all the clouds of heaven;
Yet here no fishermen for shelter look
When sailing home at even:--
'Tis that there are no sandy reaches,
Nor sheltering beaches,
Where the frail craft might find some shelt'ring nook.
Ah, well-a-day! we have no sandy reaches:--
But heed that not;
Nor shelving beaches:--
But heed that not!
Come a-jostling and a-hustling
O'er our billows gayly bustling:--
Come, all ye boats, and anchor in this spot!
Anon.

poems.title: Lines to a Friend
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Japan is not a land where men need pray,
For 'tis itself divine:--
Yet do I lift my voice in prayer and say:--
"May ev'ry joy be thine!
And may I too, if thou those joys attain,
Live on to see thee blest!"
Such the fond prayer, that, like the restless main,
Will rise within my breast.
Hitomaro.

poems.title: A Very Ancient Ode
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Mountains and ocean-waves
Around me lie;
Forever the mountain-chains
Tower to the sky;
Fixed is the ocean
Immutably:--
Man is a thing of nought,
Born but to die!
Anon.

poems.title: The Bridge to Heaven[150]
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: Oh! that that ancient bridge,
Hanging 'twixt heaven and earth, were longer still!
Oh! that yon tow'ring mountain-ridge
So boldly tow'ring, tow'red more boldly still!
Then from the moon on high
I'd fetch some drops of the life-giving stream--
A gift that might beseem
Our Lord, the King, to make him live for aye!
Anon.

poems.title: Couplet
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: When the great men of old pass'd by this way,
Could e'en their pleasures vie with ours to-day?
Anon.
FOOTNOTES:
[Footnote 148: One of the ancient names of Japan, given to the country
on account of a supposed resemblance in shape to that insect. The
dragon-flies of Japan are various and very beautiful.]
[Footnote 149: The Mikado referred to is Zhiyomei, who died in A.D.
[Footnote 150: The poet alludes to the so-called Ama-no-Ukihashi, or
"floating bridge of heaven"--the bridge by which, according to the
Japanese mythology, the gods passed up and down in the days of old.]

poems.title: Dramatis Personae
poems.author: Classical Japanese poets
lines: MITSUNAKA, Lord of the Horse to the Emperor Murakami.
BIJIYAU, Son of Mitsunaka, and still a boy.
NAKAMITSU, retainer of Mitsunaka.
KAUZHIYU, son of Nakamitsu, and foster-brother of Bijiyau.
WESHIN, Abbot of the great monastery on Mount Hiyei, near Kiyauto
(Miaco).
The Chorus.
Scene.--The Temple of Chiynuzanzhi, and my Lord Mitsunaka's palace in
Kiyauto.
Time.--Early in the Tenth Century.

poems.title: To Captain H-----D, of the 65th Regiment
poems.author: Phillis Wheatley
lines: To Captain H-----D, of the 65th Regiment.
SAY, muse divine, can hostile scenes delight
The warrior's bosom in the fields of fight?
Lo! here the christian and the hero join
With mutual grace to form the man divine.
In H-----D see with pleasure and surprise,
Where valour kindles, and where virtue lies:
Go, hero brave, still grace the post of fame,
And add new glories to thine honour'd name,
Still to the field, and still to virtue true:
Britannia glories in no son like you.

book.title: Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral

poems.title: Vashti
poems.author: Frances E. W. Harper
lines: It is something, yes, all, for us to stand
Clasping by faith our Saviour's hand;
To learn to labor, live and fight
On the side of God and changeless light.

poems.title: The Refiner'S Gold
poems.author: Frances E. W. Harper
lines: I ask to clasp their hands again
'Mid the holy hosts of heaven,
Enraptured say: "I am here, oh! God,
"And the children Thou hast given."

poems.title: [Illustration: MARY E. HARPER.]
poems.author: Frances E. W. Harper
lines: [Illustration: MARY E. HARPER.]
[Illustration: Frances E. W. Harper.]

poems.title: God Bless Our Native Land
poems.author: Frances E. W. Harper
lines: Land of the newly free,
Oh may she ever stand
For truth and liberty.
God bless our native land,
Where sleep our kindred dead,
Let peace at thy command
Above their graves be shed.
God help our native land,
Bring surcease to her strife,
And shower from thy hand
A more abundant life.
God bless our native land,
Her homes and children bless,
Oh may she ever stand
For truth and righteousness.

poems.title: Renewal of Strength
poems.author: Frances E. W. Harper
lines: The prison-house in which I live
Is falling to decay,
But God renews my spirit’s strength,
Within these walls of clay.
For me a dimness slowly creeps
Around earth’s fairest light,
But heaven grows clearer to my view,
And fairer to my sight.
It may be earth’s sweet harmonies
Are duller to my ear,
But music from my Father’s house
Begins to float more near.
Then let the pillars of my home
Crumble and fall away;
Lo, God’s dear love within my soul
Renews it day by day.

poems.title: A Plaint
poems.author: Alice Dunbar-Nelson
lines: Dear God, 'tis hard, so awful hard to lose
The one we love, and see him go afar,
With scarce one thought of aching hearts behind,
Nor wistful eyes, nor outstretched yearning hands.
Chide not, dear God, if surging thoughts arise.
And bitter questionings of love and fate,
But rather give my weary heart thy rest,
And turn the sad, dark memories into sweet.
Dear God, I fain my loved one were anear,
But since thou will'st that happy thence he'll be,
I send him forth, and back I'll choke the grief
Rebellious rises in my lonely heart.
I pray thee, God, my loved one joy to bring;
I dare not hope that joy will be with me,
But ah, dear God, one boon I crave of thee,
That he shall ne'er forget his hours with me.

poems.title: If I Had Known
poems.author: Alice Dunbar-Nelson
lines: Two years ago how drear this life should be,
And crowd upon itself allstrangely sad,
Mayhap another song would burst from out my lips,
Overflowing with the happiness of future hopes;
Mayhap another throb than that of joy.
Have stirred my soul into its inmost depths,
If I had known.
If I had known,
Two years ago the impotence of love,
The vainness of a kiss, how barren a caress,
Mayhap my soul to higher things have soarn,
Nor clung to earthly loves and tender dreams,
But ever up aloft into the blue empyrean,
And there to master all the world of mind,
If I had known.

poems.title: Love and the Butterfly
poems.author: Alice Dunbar-Nelson
lines: I heard a merry voice one day
And glancing at my side,
Fair Love, all breathless, flushed with play,
A butterfly did ride.
"Whither away, oh sportive boy?"
I asked, he tossed his head;
Laughing aloud for purest joy,
And past me swiftly sped.
Next day I heard a plaintive cry
And Love crept in my arms;
Weeping he held the butterfly,
Devoid of all its charms.
Sweet words of comfort, whispered I
Into his dainty ears,
But Love still hugged the butterfly,
And bathed its wounds with tears.

poems.title: Amid the Roses
poems.author: Alice Dunbar-Nelson
lines: There is tropical warmth and languorous life
Where the roses lie
In a tempting drift
Of pink and red and golden light
Untouched as yet by the pruning knife.
And the still, warm life of the roses fair
That whisper "Come,"
With promises
Of sweet caresses, close and pure
Has a thorny whiff in the perfumed air.
There are thorns and love in the roses' bed,
And Satan too
Must linger there;
So Satan's wiles and the conscience stings,
Must now abide--the roses are dead.

poems.title: Ships That Pass in the Night
poems.author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
lines: Out in the sky the great dark clouds are massing;
I look far out into the pregnant night,
Where I can hear a solemn booming gun
And catch the gleaming of a random light,
That tells me that the ship I seek is passing, passing.
My tearful eyes my soul's deep hurt are glassing;
For I would hail and check that ship of ships.
I stretch my hands imploring, cry aloud,
My voice falls dead a foot from mine own lips,
And but its ghost doth reach that vessel, passing, passing.
O Earth, O Sky, O Ocean, both surpassing,
O heart of mine, O soul that dreads the dark!
Is there no hope for me? Is there no way
That I may sight and check that speeding bark
Which out of sight and sound is passing, passing?

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: The Debt
poems.author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
lines: This is the debt I pay
Just for one riotous day,
Years of regret and grief.
Sorrow without relief.
Pay it I will to the end--
Until the grave, my friend,
Gives me a true release--
Gives me the clasp of peace.
Slight was the thing I bought,
Small was the debt I thought,
Poor was the loan at best--
God! but the interest!

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: A Death Song
poems.author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
lines: Lay me down beneaf de willers in de grass,
Whah de branch'll go a-singin' as it pass
An' w'en I's a-layin' low,
I kin hyeah it as it go
Singin', "Sleep, my honey, tek yo' res' at las'."
Lay me nigh to whah hit meks a little pool,
An' de watah stan's so quiet lak an' cool,
Whah de little birds in spring,
Ust to come an' drink an' sing,
An' de chillen waded on dey way to school.
Let me settle w'en my shouldahs draps dey load
Nigh enough to hyeah de noises in de road;
Fu' I t'ink de las' long res'
Gwine to soothe my sperrit bes'
If I's layin' 'mong de t'ings I's allus knowed.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Negro Serenade
poems.author: James Edwin Campbell
lines: O, de light-bugs glimmer down de lane,
Merlindy! Merlindy!
O, de whip'-will callin' notes ur pain--
Merlindy, O, Merlindy!
O, honey lub, my turkle dub,
Doan' you hyuh my bawnjer ringin',
While de night-dew falls an' de ho'n owl calls
By de ol' ba'n gate Ise singin'.
O, Miss 'Lindy, doan' you hyuh me, chil',
Merlindy! Merlindy!
My lub fur you des dribe me wil'--
Merlindy, O, Merlindy!
I'll sing dis night twel broad day-light,
Ur bu's' my froat wid tryin',
'Less you come down, Miss 'Lindy Brown,
An' stops dis ha't f'um sighin'!

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: The Negro Singer
poems.author: James D. Corrothers
lines: O'er all my song the image of a face
Lieth, like shadow on the wild sweet flowers.
The dream, the ecstasy that prompts my powers;
The golden lyre's delights bring little grace
To bless the singer of a lowly race.
Long hath this mocked me: aye in marvelous hours,
When Hera's gardens gleamed, or Cynthia's bowers,
Or Hope's red pylons, in their far, hushed place!
But I shall dig me deeper to the gold;
Fetch water, dripping, over desert miles,
From clear Nyanzas and mysterious Niles
Of love; and sing, nor one kind act withhold.
So shall men know me, and remember long,
Nor my dark face dishonor any song.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: A Butterfly in Church
poems.author: Daniel Webster Davis
lines: What dost thou here, thou shining, sinless thing,
With many colored hues and shapely wing?
Why quit the open field and summer air
To flutter here? Thou hast no need of prayer.
'Tis meet that we, who this great structure built,
Should come to be redeemed and washed from guilt,
For we this gilded edifice within
Are come, with erring hearts and stains of sin.
But thou art free from guilt as God on high;
Go, seek the blooming waste and open sky,
And leave us here our secret woes to bear,
Confessionals and agonies of prayer.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Sandy Star and Willie Gee
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: Count 'em two, you make 'em three:
Pluck the man and boy apart
And you'll see into my heart.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Del Cascar
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: Del Cascar, Del Cascar,
Stood upon a flaming star,
Stood, and let his feet hang down
Till in China the toes turned brown.
And he reached his fingers over
The rim of the sea, like sails from Dover,
And caught a Mandarin at prayer,
And tickled his nose in Orion's hair.
The sun went down through crimson bars,
And left his blind face battered with stars--
But the brown toes in China kept
Hot the tears Del Cascar wept.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Turn Me to My Yellow Leaves
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: I am better satisfied;
There is something in me grieves--
That was never born, and died.
Let me be a scarlet flame
On a windy autumn morn,
I who never had a name,
Nor from breathing image born.
From the margin let me fall
Where the farthest stars sink down,
And the void consumes me,--all
In nothingness to drown.
Let me dream my dream entire,
Withered as an autumn leaf--
Let me have my vain desire,
Vain--as it is brief.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Ironic: Ll.d
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: There are no hollows any more
Between the mountains; the prairie floor
Is like a curtain with the drape
Of the winds' invisible shape;
And nowhere seen and nowhere heard
The sea's quiet as a sleeping bird.
Now we're traveling, what holds back
Arrival, in the very track
Where the urge put forth; so we stay
And move a thousand miles a day.
Time's a Fancy ringing bells
Whose meaning, charlatan history, tells!

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Scintilla
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: I kissed a kiss in youth
Upon a dead man's brow;
And that was long ago,--
And I'm a grown man now.
It's lain there in the dust,
Thirty years and more;--
My lips that set a light
At a dead man's door.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Sic Vita
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: Heart free, hand free,
Blue above, brown under,
All the world to me
Is a place of wonder.
Sun shine, moon shine,
Stars, and winds a-blowing,
All into this heart of mine
Flowing, flowing, flowing!
Mind free, step free,
Days to follow after,
Joys of life sold to me
For the price of laughter.
Girl's love, man's love,
Love of work and duty,
Just a will of God's to prove
Beauty, beauty, beauty!

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Rhapsody
poems.author: William Stanley Braithwaite
lines: I am glad daylong for the gift of song,
For time and change and sorrow;
For the sunset wings and the world-end things
Which hang on the edge of to-morrow.
I am glad for my heart whose gates apart
Are the entrance-place of wonders,
Where dreams come in from the rush and din
Like sheep from the rains and thunders.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Sence You Went Away
poems.author: James Weldon Johnson
lines: Seems lak to me de stars don't shine so bright,
Seems lak to me de sun done loss his light,
Seems lak to me der's nothin' goin' right,
Sence you went away.
Seems lak to me de sky ain't half so blue,
Seems lak to me dat ev'ything wants you,
Seems lak to me I don't know what to do,
Sence you went away.
Seems lak to me dat ev'ything is wrong,
Seems lak to me de day's jes twice es long,
Seems lak to me de bird's forgot his song,
Sence you went away.
Seems lak to me I jes can't he'p but sigh,
Seems lak to me ma th'oat keeps gittin' dry,
Seems lak to me a tear stays in ma eye,
Sence you went away.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Mother Night
poems.author: James Weldon Johnson
lines: Eternities before the first-born day,
Or ere the first sun fledged his wings of flame,
Calm Night, the everlasting and the same,
A brooding mother over chaos lay.
And whirling suns shall blaze and then decay,
Shall run their fiery courses and then claim
The haven of the darkness whence they came;
Back to Nirvanic peace shall grope their way.
So when my feeble sun of life burns out,
And sounded is the hour for my long sleep,
I shall, full weary of the feverish light,
Welcome the darkness without fear or doubt,
And heavy-lidded, I shall softly creep
Into the quiet bosom of the Night.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: Tuskegee
poems.author: Leslie Pinckney Hill
lines: Wherefore this busy labor without rest?
Is it an idle dream to which we cling,
Here where a thousand dusky toilers sing
Unto the world their hope? "Build we our best.
By hand and thought," they cry, "although unblessed."
So the great engines throb, and anvils ring,
And so the thought is wedded to the thing;
But what shall be the end, and what the test?
Dear God, we dare not answer, we can see
Not many steps ahead, but this we know--
If all our toilsome building is in vain,
Availing not to set our manhood free,
If envious hate roots out the seed we sow,
The South will wear eternally a stain.

book.title: The Book of American Negro Poetry (ed. James Weldon Johnson)

poems.title: The Teacher
poems.author: Leslie Pinckney Hill
lines: Lord, who am I to teach the way
To little children day by day,
So prone myself to go astray?
